subject: Roadmap sprint gaps & contingency plan for QBR
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, tessa.morgan@redwood.com; Jamie Lee <jamie.lee@acme-retail.com>; Priya Shah <priya.shah@marketplace.org>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Roadmap sprint gaps & contingency plan for QBR

Team — attaching a short mitigation matrix and a proposed contingency outline ahead of Wednesday's QBR prep. High-level asks: please review, confirm owners, and flag any uncontrollable dependencies by EOD tomorrow.

Top concerns I'm seeing across product & engineering:
- Feature scope creep: two feature stories (Search relevance tuning, Multi-tenant routing) are slipping by ~3 sprints.
- Infra fragility: nightly worker OOMs on longer contexts causing intermittent rollbacks (infra team tracking but needs escalation).
- Third-party dependency: Acme's integration tests are delayed, which blocks end-to-end validation for the retail adapter.
- Model regression risk: recent quantized build shows small BLEU/regression in internal evals — may require rollback or canary.

Proposed immediate moves (in doc):
1) Scope freeze for non-blocking UX polish (owner: laura_bennett)
2) Temporary route to smaller model variant for high-throughput endpoints (owner: vivek_kulkarni)
3) Prioritize infra hotfix and increase burn-down visibility (owner: karthik_iyer)
4) Ask partner (Acme) for a fixed test window this week; Jamie/Priya can help triage on their side.

Attachments: qbr_mitigation_matrix.xlsx, sprint-burndown.png (see Drive).

I'm copying the customer contacts so they can see the plan and confirm test windows. If you disagree with owners above, reply with changes.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
VP, Product
Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: jordan.blake@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: tessa.morgan@redwood.com; Jamie Lee <jamie.lee@acme-retail.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Roadmap sprint gaps & contingency plan for QBR

Jordan — thanks for the summary and the matrix. Quick thoughts:

On model regression: we should prepare a canary traffic split (90/10) to the quantized build and measure quality on the production prompt set for at least 24 hours before any rollback. If we see delta > 3% on our primary eval, auto-fallback to the previous variant. I can own the canary config and monitoring hooks.

On infra: Karthik, I recommend a temporary scale-up of the worker fleet for the next 48 hours and a short SLA exception with SRE to prioritize the OOM hotfix. That will buy time while we validate the model canary.

On scope: Agree with a freeze on non-blocking UX work. Laura — can you produce a minimal scope list (MVP items only) by EOD tomorrow so product can re-slice the roadmap?

Related: EPIC-4523 has the end-to-end test cases that Acme must sign off on. Jamie, can you confirm a window this Wed/Thu?

Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Roadmap sprint gaps & contingency plan for QBR

Jordan / Vivek — attaching the sprint burndown image for the last three sprints and a short blocker list below. I pulled velocity numbers for the team so we can be concrete in the QBR.

Current snapshot:
- Avg sprint velocity (story points) last 3 sprints: 145 -> 132 -> 118 (down ~14% sprint-over-sprint).
- Two P0 blockers: (1) Multi-tenant routing test harness failing intermittently (flaky mocks), (2) Nightly worker OOM on long-context replays (linked logs in EPIC-4523).
- Risk window: next 10 business days — if both issues persist we'll miss the soft-launch date by at least two weeks.

Mitigations in flight:
- Triage session scheduled with SRE today at 11:00 (owner: karthik_iyer).
- Temporary scope reduction list attached (I marked which stories are safe to drop).
- Candidate rollback plan: revert to prior routing branch that doesn't include the experimental cache; that'll remove 1 failing story but costs ~5% latency increase.

Actionable asks:
1) Jordan — confirm freeze boundary (which stories we treat as must-deliver vs deferrable).
2) Karhtik — escalate OOM patch; if SRE needs headroom, please request a soft capacity commit from Infra.
3) Jamie/Priya — please confirm test window for integration (Thu 8–10am PT preferred).

Date: Wed, 07 Apr 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Finalizing contingency plan for QBR — need confirmations

Thanks everyone for the fast responses. Summary and next steps below — I'm going to present this as the contingency section in tomorrow's QBR pack unless there are objections. Please reply with any changes within the next 12 hours.

Decisions agreed:
- Scope freeze: non-MVP items pulled from the release train; Laura to send finalized freeze list by EOD Thu.
- Canary: Vivek to own a 90/10 canary for the quantized build; automatic fallback if primary eval delta > 3%.
- Infra: Karhtik to request a 48-72 hour capacity uplift from Infra and lead the OOM hotfix triage.
- Partner tests: Jamie/Priya to confirm Thu 8–10am PT window; if unavailable, fallback is Fri 10–12 PT.

Deliverables and owners:
- qbr_mitigation_matrix.xlsx (completed) — Jordan
- Final freeze list (doc) — Laura
- Canary config + dashboards — Vivek
- Infra capacity request + patch ETA — Karhtik

Meeting: I've added a short sync in calendars for Thu 9:00am PT to validate the test window and confirm the freeze list: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=qbr-prep-briefing

If no objections, I'll lock this plan and update the QBR pack.

Jordan Blake
VP, Product
Redwood Inference
